memberdef.argsstring: (XFlash *InstancePtr, u32 BaseAddress, u8 BusWidth, int IsPlatformFlash)
memberdef.name: XFlash_Initialize

detaileddescription.para:
The initialization entails:
Check the Device family type.
Issuing the CFI query command.
Get and translate relevant CFI query information.
Set default options for the instance.
Setup the VTable.
Call the family initialize function of the instance.
Initialize the Xilinx Platform Flash XL to Async mode if the application selects to use the Platform Flash XL in the MLD. The Platform Flash XL is an Intel CFI compliant device.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XFlash instance.
Base address of the flash memory.
Total width of the flash memory, in bytes.
Used to specify if the flash is a platform flash.

listitem.para: XFLASH_PART_NOT_SUPPORTED if the command set algorithm or Layout is not supported by any flash family compiled into the system.

XFLASH_CFI_QUERY_ERROR if the device would not enter CFI query mode. Either the devices lack CFI support, the wrong BaseAddress param was used, an unsupported part layout exists, or a hardware problem exists with the part.

simplesect.para: BusWidth is not the width of an individual part. It is the total operating width. For example, if there are two 16-bit parts, with one tied to data lines D0-D15 and other tied to D16-D31, BusWidth would be (32 / 8) = 4. If a single 16-bit flash is in 8-bit mode, then BusWidth should be (8 / 8) = 1.

briefdescription.para: Resets the flash device and places it in read mode.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XFlash instance.

listitem.para: XFLASH_BUSY if the flash devices were in the middle of an operation and could not be reset.
XFLASH_ERROR if the devices have experienced an internal error during the operation. XFlash_DeviceControl() must be used to access the cause of the device specific error condition.

Device specific command to issue.
Specifies the arguments passed to the device control function.

briefdescription.para: Reads data from the Flash device into the specified buffer.

detaileddescription.para: Reads the data from the Flash device and copies it into the specified destination buffer.
The source and destination addresses can be on any alignment supported by the processor.
The device is polled until an error or the operation completes successfully.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XFlash instance.
Offset into the device address space from which to read.
Number of bytes to copy.
Destination address to copy data to.

listitem.para: XFLASH_ADDRESS_ERROR if the source address does not start within the addressable areas of the devices.

simplesect.para: This function allows the transfer of data past the end of the device's address space. If this occurs, then results are undefined.

briefdescription.para: Programs the flash devices with data specified in the source buffer.

detaileddescription.para: The source and destination address must be aligned to the width of the flash's data bus.
The device is polled until an error or the operation completes successfully.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XFlash instance.
Offset into the device address space from which to begin programming. Must be aligned to the width of the flash's data bus.
Number of bytes to program.

Source address containing data to be programmed. Must be aligned to the width of the flash's data bus. The SrcPtr does not have to be aligned to the flash width if the processor supports unaligned access. But this library is generic, and some processors (for example, MicroBlaze) do not support unaligned access. So this API requires the SrcPtr to be aligned.

listitem.para: XFLASH_ERROR if a write error occurred. This error is usually device specific. Use XFlash_DeviceControl() to retrieve specific error conditions. When this error is returned, it is possible that the target address range was only partially programmed.

briefdescription.para: Erases the specified address range in the flash device.

detaileddescription.para: The number of bytes to erase can be any number as long as it is within the bounds of the devices.
The device is polled until an error or the operation completes successfully.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XFlash instance.
Offset into the device address space from which to begin erasure.
Number of bytes to erase.

listitem.para: XFLASH_ADDRESS_ERROR if the destination address range is not completely within the addressable areas of the devices.

simplesect.para: Due to flash memory design, the range actually erased may be larger than what was specified by the Offset & Bytes parameters. This occurs if the parameters do not align to block boundaries.

briefdescription.para: Locks the blocks in the specified range of the flash devices.

detaileddescription.para: The device is polled until an error or the operation completes successfully.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XFlash instance.

Offset into the device address space from which to begin block locking. The first three bytes of every block are reserved for a special purpose. The offset should be at least three bytes from the start of the block.
Number of bytes to lock in the block starting from Offset.

listitem.para: XFLASH_ADDRESS_ERROR if the destination address range is not completely within the addressable areas of the devices.

simplesect.para: Due to flash memory design, the range actually locked may be larger than what was specified by the Offset & Bytes parameters. This occurs if the parameters do not align to block boundaries.

briefdescription.para: Unlocks the blocks in the specified range of the flash devices.

detaileddescription.para: The device is polled until an error or the operation completes successfully.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XFlash instance.

Offset into the device address space from which to begin block UnLocking. The first three bytes of every block are reserved for a special purpose. The offset should be at least three bytes from the start of the block.
Number of bytes to unlock in the block starting from Offset.

listitem.para: XFLASH_ADDRESS_ERROR if the destination address range is not completely within the addressable areas of the devices.

briefdescription.para: Defines the XFlash library interface for CFI flash memory devices.

detaileddescription.para: This module implements the functionality for flash memory devices that conform to the "Common Flash Interface" (CFI) standard. CFI allows a single flash library to be used for an entire family of parts.
This is not a library for a specific device, but for a set of command read/write/erase algorithms. CFI allows the library to determine which algorithm to use at runtime.

The application should call XFlash_Initialize() before any other function in the library. The initialization function checks for the device family and initializes the XFlash instance with the family specific data. It sets up the VT table, which contains the function pointers to the family specific APIs, and calls the family specific initialization routine.

The Device geometry varies for different flash device families. The following list describes geometry of different flash device families: Intel Flash Device Geometry Flash memory space is segmented into areas called blocks. The size of each block is based on a power of 2. A region is defined as a contiguous set of blocks of the same size. Some parts have several regions while others have one. This module refers to the arrangement of blocks and regions as the part's geometry. Some Intel flash supports multiple banks on the same device. This library supports single and multiple bank flash devices. AMD Flash Device Geometry Flash memory space is segmented into areas called banks and further into regions and blocks. The size of each block is based on a power of 2. A region is defined as a contiguous set of blocks of the same size. Some parts have several regions while others have one. A bank is defined as a contiguous set of blocks. The bank may contain blocks of different size. This module refers to the arrangement of blocks, regions and banks as the part's geometry. The cells within the part can be programmed from a logic 1 to a logic 0 and not the other way around. To change a cell back to a logic 1, the entire block containing that cell must be erased. When a block is erased all bytes contain the value 0xFF. The number of times a block can be erased is finite. Eventually the block wears out and is no longer capable of erasure. As of this writing, the typical flash block can be erased 100,000 or more times.

The write call writes a minimum of zero bytes and a maximum of the entire flash. An error is reported back to the caller if the Offset Address specified to write is out of flash. An error is also reported if the number of bytes specified from the Offset address exceeds flash boundaries. The write is blocking in nature: control returns to the caller only after the write operation completes successfully or an error is reported.

The read call reads a minimum of zero bytes and a maximum of the entire flash. If the Offset Address specified to read is out of flash boundary, an error is reported back to the caller. The read function reads memory locations beyond Flash boundary. Make sure that the Number of Bytes + Offset address is within the Flash address boundaries. The read is blocking in nature: control returns to the caller only after the read operation completes successfully or an error is reported.

The erase operations erase a Block in the Flash memory. The erase call is blocking in nature: control returns to the caller only after the erase operation completes successfully or an error is reported.
The Flash Device is divided into Blocks. Each Block can be protected individually from unwarranted writing/erasing.

Use the XFlash_Lock() call to lock blocks. All the memory locations from the specified Offset address are locked. Use the XFlash_Unlock() call to unlock blocks. All the Blocks which are previously locked are unlocked.
The Lock and Unlock calls are blocking in nature: control returns to the caller only after the operation completes successfully or an error is reported.

The AMD flash device requires high voltage on the Reset pin to perform lock and unlock operations. Provide this high voltage (as defined in the datasheet) to the reset pin before calling the lock and unlock APIs for AMD flash devices. Lock and Unlock features are not tested for AMD flash devices.
Functionalities specific to a Flash Device Family are implemented as Device Control.

The following are the Intel specific device control:
Retrieve the last error data.
Get Device geometry.
Get Device properties.
Set RYBY pin mode.
Set the Configuration register (Platform Flash only).

The following are the AMD specific device control:
Get Device geometry.
Get Device properties.
Erase Resume.
Erase Suspend.
Enter Extended Mode.
Exit Extended Mode.
Get Protection Status of Block Group.
Erase Chip.

simplesect.para:
This library needs to know the type of EMC core (AXI or XPS) used to access the cfi flash, to map the correct APIs. Use this library with the emc driver, v3_01_a and above, so that this information can be automatically obtained from the emc driver.
This library is intended to be RTOS and processor independent. It works with physical addresses only. The layer above this library must satisfy any needs for dynamic memory management, threads, mutual exclusion, virtual memory, cache control, or HW write protection management.
All writes to flash occur in units of bus-width bytes. If more than one part exists on the data bus, then the parts are written in parallel. Reads from flash are performed in any width up to the width of the data bus. The library assumes that the flash bus controller or local bus supports these types of accesses.
